headline: BARRICK SPLITS IN TWO: FILES FOR $42B AMERICAN BARRICK GOLD IPO ON NYSE — NEVADA, PUEBLO VIEJO INTO NEW CO
snippet: Barrick Mining filed its S-1 registration statement on November 10 to take its North American gold assets public as American Barrick Gold Corporation (NYSE: ABGC), separating the Nevada Gold Mines joint-venture complex (Carlin, Cortez, Turquoise Ridge) and Pueblo Viejo in the Dominican Republic into a standalone company led by CEO Mark Hill. Analysts estimate the new entity could be valued at up to $42 billion — with Newmont consenting to the spin after receiving $1.95 billion from Barrick — in what would be the largest mining equity event of 2026 and a defining test of North American investor appetite for large-cap gold.

headline: GOLD REBOUNDS TO $4,057, SILVER SURGES 2.9% TO $53 ON NOV 11 — RELIEF RALLY FROM CPI-DRIVEN ROUT
snippet: Gold spot recovered to approximately $4,057 per ounce on November 11 — up roughly $37 from Monday's CPI-driven close — while silver jumped 2.9% to $53.01, partly reversing last week's sharp losses as thinner Remembrance Day volumes allowed dip-buyers back in. The rebound does not yet challenge the $3,886 support level flagged by Standard Chartered, but the size of silver's one-day move suggests the gold-silver ratio stretched to around 76.5x is attracting contrarian positioning.

headline: TUDOR GOLD HITS 9.5M AT 9.00 G/T AU AT TREATY CREEK PERFECTSTORM — 43 G/T INCLUDED, NEW SYSTEM 500M AWAY
snippet: Tudor Gold (TSX-V: TUD) reported that hole PS-26-36 at the Perfectstorm Zone of its Treaty Creek project in British Columbia returned 9.50 metres grading 9.00 g/t gold, including a 1.20-metre interval of 43.29 g/t — headline grades that rank among the best single-hole results at a project already hosting one of Canada's largest undeveloped gold-copper systems. More significantly, the company identified a new high-grade system approximately 500 metres northwest of prior drilling, with 19 holes still awaiting assays.

headline: NOVAGOLD SETS DEC 1 DONLIN GOLD CLOSE — NYSE LISTING AS 'NG' ON DEC 2, TSX DELISTED
snippet: NOVAGOLD Resources announced on November 10 that it expects to acquire Paulson's remaining 40% stake in Donlin Gold on December 1, taking sole ownership of a 39-million-ounce undeveloped gold project in Alaska — one of the world's largest — before listing the reorganized company, NovaGold Corporation, on the NYSE under its existing ticker 'NG' at the opening of trading on December 2 and delisting from the TSX. The structure follows shareholder approval on November 4 (69.15% of outstanding shares represented) and court approval on November 9.

headline: CHINA EXTENDS RARE EARTH EXPORT CONTROLS PAUSE TO JAN 10, 2027 — NOVEMBER 10 DEADLINE AVERTED
snippet: China announced on November 9 a two-month extension of the suspension of its October 2025 rare earth and battery export controls, pushing the new expiry to January 10, 2027 — one day before the prior pause was due to expire. Critically, the April 2025 licensing regime remains in force: the extension removes the near-term escalation risk for Western manufacturers and rare earth producers like MP Materials and Energy Fuels, but it does not remove the structural overhang that depressed USAR, MP and UUUU by 5–11% on November 10.

headline: NVRO METALS RAISES C$35.8M TO ACQUIRE NORTHERN TERRITORIES RESOURCES — CLOSING NOV 13
snippet: NVRO Metals completed a C$35.8 million private placement to fund its acquisition of Northern Territories Resources, with the deal expected to close on or about November 13 following regulatory clearances. The transaction consolidates an Australian copper-gold exploration and development portfolio under NVRO's banner, adding Northern Territories' assets to its existing pipeline at a time when copper M&A activity has accelerated against a backdrop of SHFE warehouse stocks near three-year lows.

headline: LME COPPER SLIDES TO $13,840/T — YANGSHAN PREMIUM HITS RECORD $230/T AS CHINA BUYS HAND-TO-MOUTH
snippet: LME copper fell further to US$13,840 per tonne on November 11 as macro headwinds from US rate-hike expectations continued to weigh, even as the Shanghai Yangshan copper premium surged to a record US$230 per tonne — a figure that tells a structurally bullish story about physical tightness inside China: manufacturers are procuring hand-to-mouth because the premium makes it uneconomic to hold inventory, compressing orders but not reducing underlying demand. The divergence between weak futures prices and record physical premiums is a key data point for copper equity investors navigating the current risk-off environment.

headline: TROILUS DRILLS 34M AT 1.33 G/T AuEq AT Z87, QUEBEC — GOLD FOUND IN CURRENT WASTE ZONE COULD BOOST RESOURCE
snippet: Troilus Gold reported that hole 87-26-524 at its Z87 deposit in Quebec returned 34 metres averaging 1.33 g/t gold equivalent, including 12 metres at 3.08 g/t — notably, from rock the current mine plan classifies as waste. The company notes 2026 drilling is excluded from existing resource estimates, meaning this result directly expands the economic case for a project already carrying a large in-pit resource and advanced permitting, with the discovery of payable gold in what the mine plan treats as internal dilution representing a potential uplift to project economics.

headline: WHY GOLD MINERS FALL 2-3X HARDER THAN GOLD — OPERATING LEVERAGE ANALYSIS OF THE NOVEMBER RECKONING
snippet: Discovery Alert's November analysis explains why mining equities consistently lose two to three times as much as the spot metal in a correction: fixed operating costs mean every dollar drop in realized gold price falls directly to the bottom line, while exploration-stage juniors face the additional squeeze of compressed financing windows and rising real discount rates. Rick Rule and Jeff Phillips are quoted arguing that this operating-leverage gap — currently 30-40% below the 2026 equity highs versus a metal that remains near $4,000 — is precisely where multi-year entry opportunities appear for investors who can tolerate short-term drawdowns.

headline: GOLD-SILVER RATIO AT 76.5X — SILVER SHOULD BE $58.60 IF RATIO REVERTS TO 69.2X HISTORICAL MEAN
snippet: With gold at approximately $4,057 and silver at $53, the gold-silver ratio stands near 76.5x — well above its trailing mean of 69.2x, which GoldSeek's column uses to calculate that silver is currently 10-12% below where it 'should' trade relative to gold if the ratio normalizes. Physical silver market tightness that drove the ratio below 68x in early 2026 has since eased; the analysis argues the current ratio expansion reflects temporary macro headwinds rather than a structural shift, and that silver's industrial-and-monetary dual demand profile makes it a higher-beta recovery play than gold when rate-hike fears recede.

headline: MOTLEY FOOL: NEWMONT $4,546/OZ REALIZED GOLD, FRANCO-NEVADA ROYALTY MODEL — 3 MINING STOCKS TO OWN EITHER WAY
snippet: A November 8 Motley Fool analysis walks through where gold and copper prices may head from current levels and identifies three mining stocks offering asymmetric exposure: Newmont, which delivered a $4,546 per ounce realized gold price in Q3 2026 (up 29% year-over-year), Franco-Nevada's royalty-and-streaming model that provides gold leverage without direct operating cost exposure, and Freeport-McMoRan for investors who believe copper's physical tightness — visible in record Yangshan premiums — will re-price the metal above near-term macro headwinds. The piece argues that investors who are unsure of the macro direction can structure a position across all three to capture the commodity upside without betting on the direction of real rates.
